title: The Gardener of the Nation: Paris, the Palermo Garden, and the Parks of the Republic
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: The Rue and the Nursery: Paris Before Argentina

stops.name: Paris, the typographer's son
stops.date_confidence: attested by the Buenos Aires Historical Archive biography for 20 August 1849; the street and the arrondissement of the birth were not located in any reachable source, so the pin is the canonical city point
stops.campa: A son is born to Simon Thays, a typographer out of Belgium, and to Ernestine Paris, of a Versailles commercial family, and is registered Jules Charles. The city around the cradle is about to be torn open: within four years Haussmann begins cutting boulevards through it, and Adolphe Alphand begins planting the parks that come with them, the Bois de Boulogne, the Buttes-Chaumont, the squares set into every quarter. The boy will spend his working life doing to another capital what is being done to this one. No record gives the street.
suggested_refs: The Second Empire park works of Adolphe Alphand, contemporaneous with Thays's Paris childhood
sources: Buenos Aires Historical Archive, 'Quién fue Carlos Thays' (buenosaires.gob.ar)
es.wikipedia.org, 'Carlos Thays'

stops.name: Saint-Germain-des-Prés, the baptism at ten
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. Family recollection reported in La Nación (2018) has the father dead when the boy was seven and the baptism at ten, which puts it around 1859; no parish register was reached, the La Nación page returned 404 during this research, and month and day default to 01
stops.campa: The father dies when the boy is seven, family memory holds, and the boy is carried to the font only at ten, years late by the custom of the quarter. He is christened Jules Charles, the name he will spend in French and sign in Spanish as Carlos. The church above him is the oldest in Paris, an abbey older than the kingdom, one square tower left of it. Nothing else of the childhood survives in any reachable source: no school, no address, no account of how a fatherless boy came to the nursery trade.
suggested_refs: The parish registers of Saint-Germain-des-Prés, not consulted for this journey
sources: La Nación (2018), 'Carlos Thays, el francés que le dio color a los parques y estancias argentinas', reported at second hand; the page itself was unreachable

stops.name: Paris, in the office of Édouard André
stops.date_confidence: the apprenticeship is attested: the English Wikipedia article on Édouard François André calls Thays his pupil and assistant, the Spanish calls him André's secretary. Its length is not attested. The dossier's 'more than a decade' and the span c. 1870-1888 rest on no source reached here, and the year stands only to order the segment
stops.campa: He enters the office of Édouard François André: horticulturist, garden designer, plant hunter in the Andes, editor of the Revue horticole, working in the line that runs back through Barillet-Deschamps to Alphand and the parks of the Second Empire. Thays is pupil, assistant or secretary there, depending on which account you read, and how long he stayed nobody has written down. The practice is a school and an address book at once, with commissions in Luxembourg, in Uruguay, in Chile, and the standing habit of sending a trained assistant abroad when a client on another continent writes asking for a park.
suggested_refs: Édouard François André, L'Art des jardins (1879), the treatise of the office Thays trained in
sources: en.wikipedia.org, 'Édouard François André'
es.wikipedia.org, 'Carlos Thays'
La Nación (2018) profile, at second hand

stops.name: Paris, the Córdoba contract
stops.date_confidence: attested by the Buenos Aires Botanical Garden biography page for 23 May 1889. The Historical Archive dates the commission itself to 1888 and the Botanical Garden page dates his arrival in Argentina to June 1889; the three dates sit together as commission, contract, crossing, and no primary document was inspected to confirm the sequence
stops.campa: Miguel Crisol, a developer opening a new quarter south of Córdoba and calling it Nueva Córdoba, wants a park at its edge and writes to Paris for a designer. The request travels the Alphand and André network and comes to rest on an assistant of thirty-nine who has never crossed the Atlantic. The commission is dated 1888 and the contract is signed in Paris on the twenty-third of May. He is engaged for one park, in one provincial city, on the other side of the equator.
suggested_refs: The Crisol contract of 23 May 1889, cited by the Buenos Aires Botanical Garden biography
sources: Buenos Aires Botanical Garden, 'Biografía Julio Carlos Thays' (buenosaires.gob.ar)
Buenos Aires Historical Archive, 'Quién fue Carlos Thays'

stops.name: Buenos Aires, landfall
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The Botanical Garden biography gives June 1889 and the age of thirty-nine for the arrival in Argentina, but names neither port nor ship; the day defaults to 01 and the pin is the canonical Buenos Aires point rather than a documented landing place
stops.campa: He lands in a country swallowing immigrants faster than any country has managed before, most of them arriving through this port. The city he steps into is flat, treeless in its new quarters, and rich: beef and wheat pay for a ruling class that wants Paris and can order it by catalogue. Thays is one of the items ordered. The one great park is the ground Sarmiento opened at Palermo fourteen years before, and it is thin. Nobody records the ship, or the day it docked. Inland, at Córdoba, a developer is waiting for a plan of a park.
suggested_refs: The Hotel de Inmigrantes and the port of Buenos Aires in the peak decade of Argentine immigration
sources: Buenos Aires Botanical Garden, 'Biografía Julio Carlos Thays'

stops.name: Parque Crisol, Córdoba: the first Argentine plan
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction for the month. The Historical Archive dates a signed general plan to October 1889 and cites Carlos A. Page's archival study of the park, which was not inspected here; the day defaults to 01. Coordinates corrected to the es.wikipedia figure for Parque Sarmiento, the dossier's pair falling roughly 1.4 km outside the park
stops.campa: The commission is a park for a city of a hundred thousand at the foot of the sierras, and what he draws is not a square with trees in it but a landscape: lakes, curved drives, belts of planting, three square kilometres of ground held back from a grid that is still being sold in lots. He signs the general plan in October. Work starts the following year on the first seventeen hectares, on ground Miguel Crisol is paying for out of the same development that is selling the lots. In 1911 the park is renamed for Sarmiento.
suggested_refs: Carlos A. Page's archival study of Parque Sarmiento, Córdoba
sources: Buenos Aires Historical Archive, 'Quién fue Carlos Thays'
es.wikipedia.org, 'Parque Sarmiento (Córdoba)'

segments.name: Director de Paseos: the City Planted

stops.name: Municipalidad de Buenos Aires, the competition won
stops.date_confidence: attested by the Buenos Aires Historical Archive for 15 May 1891. The same page gives the twenty-two new paseos of 1891-1895 and the career totals of sixty-nine in the city and sixteen in the provinces; the dossier's comparison with twenty-seven earlier paseos appears nowhere in it and is dropped. No street address survives for the 1891 office, so the pin is the Plaza de Mayo civic core
stops.campa: An open competition is called for the direction of the city's parks and promenades, and the Frenchman two years off the boat wins it. He takes office on the fifteenth of May with the title Director de Paseos. In the first four years his department finishes twenty-two new paseos. By the end of his tenure the city archive counts sixty-nine plazas and promenades made, remade or enlarged inside the capital, and sixteen more in the provinces. He will hold the post for twenty-two years.
suggested_refs: The records of the Dirección de Paseos, Municipalidad de Buenos Aires, 1891-1913
sources: Buenos Aires Historical Archive, 'Quién fue Carlos Thays'
Buenos Aires Botanical Garden, 'Biografía Julio Carlos Thays'

stops.name: Palermo, the letter proposing a botanical garden
stops.date_confidence: attested by the Botanical Garden biography page for 22 February 1892, and the letter itself is printed in the appendices of Thays's 1910 book, verified here in the Internet Archive scan. Coordinates corrected to the es.wikipedia figure for the garden; the dossier's pair sits about 400 m northeast of a site only 350 m across
stops.campa: Ten months into the job he writes to the intendente, Francisco Bollini, proposing an acclimatization garden on municipal ground at Palermo: somewhere to test what will grow in this climate, to teach the plants of the country to the people of the city, and to give the population somewhere to walk. The letter is expediente 2661 D.1892. He asks for seven and a half hectares between Santa Fe, Las Heras and the avenue. A visit to such a place, he writes, would be at once a distraction and a powerful element of instruction for the people of Buenos Aires.
stops.quote: ...constituyendo así, con nuestras colecciones vegetales, un conjunto del cual la visita sería á la vez una distracción y un elemento poderoso de instrucción para la población bonaerense.
stops.quote_source: Carlos Thays to Intendente Francisco P. Bollini, Nota A, expediente 2661 D.1892, 22 February 1892, reproduced in El Jardín botánico de Buenos Aires (1910); a few ligature errors in the Internet Archive OCR silently corrected, wording and word order untouched
suggested_refs: Expediente 2661 D.1892, printed in the Antecedentes justificativos of Thays's 1910 book
sources: Buenos Aires Botanical Garden, 'Biografía Julio Carlos Thays'
Carlos Thays, El Jardín botánico de Buenos Aires (1910), Antecedentes justificativos, archive.org/details/eljardnbotni00buen

stops.name: Jardín Botánico, the house inside the garden
stops.date_confidence: the casona is attested: brick, Victorian, built 1881 by the engineer Jordán Wysocki, per the National Monuments Commission page. The residence is not settled: the dossier gives 1892-1898, es.wikipedia has Thays living there through the whole directorship, 1891-1913, and no source reached decides between them. The marriage to Cora Venturino carries three incompatible dates, and the hup hup story is family recollection with no contemporaneous witness
stops.campa: The family moves into the brick house already standing on the ground, put up in 1881, eleven years before the garden around it. His wife is Cora Venturino, and the marriage is a knot the record will not untie: one source gives the first of January 1892, another the thirtieth of November 1893, a third puts it earlier still by making him forty-one and her sixteen. From the door he walks each morning into a building site that is also his front garden, and the family story is that Cora calls hup, hup when she wants him to come in and eat.
suggested_refs: The 1881 casona of Jordán Wysocki, now the administration building of the Jardín Botánico
sources: argentina.gob.ar, 'Jardín Botánico Carlos Thays' (National Monuments Commission)
es.wikipedia.org, 'Jardín Botánico Carlos Thays'
contradiction flagged: three mutually inconsistent marriage dates across La Nación, a genealogical index, and es.wikipedia

stops.name: Parque 3 de Febrero, the Palermo woods enlarged
stops.date_confidence: the work spans the directorship, 1892 to 1913, per es.wikipedia and the municipal biography; 1893 is an ordering device and not an event. The Rosedal attribution is settled the other way: es.wikipedia dates it to 24 November 1914 under Benito Carrasco
stops.campa: The great park at Palermo was opened under Sarmiento in 1875, on the ground of Rosas's demolished caserón, and by the time it reaches Thays it is twenty years old and thin. He widens it, digs lakes, throws bridges, plants in belts and masses instead of rows, and pushes the boundaries out into whatever the army and the racetrack have not taken. The rose garden at its heart is not his. Benito Carrasco, who wrote his agronomy thesis under him and later took his department, opens the Rosedal on 24 November 1914.
suggested_refs: The Rosedal de Palermo, opened 24 November 1914 by Benito Javier Carrasco, routinely misattributed to Thays
sources: es.wikipedia.org, 'Carlos Thays'
Buenos Aires Botanical Garden, 'Biografía Julio Carlos Thays'
es.wikipedia.org, 'Rosedal de Palermo'

stops.name: Parque Lezama, the private garden made public
stops.date_confidence: attested by the municipal biography for 1894, the year the city acquired the Lezama grounds; month and day default to 01
stops.campa: The city buys the Lezama family's hillside garden above the old southern shoreline and hands it to his department. It is the first park he takes over rather than makes, and it is not the last. He does not start over: he lays paths through what the family planted, adds beds and ornament, and leaves the grown trees and the fall of the ground where they are, which is a different discipline from the one Palermo asks of him. Much of what visitors take for his work here was in the soil before he came to the country at all.
suggested_refs: The Lezama estate garden before municipal purchase in 1894
sources: Buenos Aires Botanical Garden, 'Biografía Julio Carlos Thays'

stops.name: Jardín Botánico, the yerbal
stops.date_confidence: attested by the Botanical Garden's own history of the yerbal collection for 1895; month and day default to 01. The hot-water treatment is described there. No dated note, paper or patent by Thays on the method was reached, and Huret's sentence quoted here is a French journalist's judgement of 1911, not a botanical source
stops.campa: Honorio Leguizamón sends him seed and cuttings of yerba mate. The cuttings die. The seed will not germinate, as it has refused to germinate for everyone who has tried since the Jesuits were expelled and the cultivated stands went back to bush. He works at it inside the garden, season after season, and finds at last that a long soak in hot water breaks whatever holds the embryo shut. Ilex paraguariensis, the plant the whole country drinks in the morning, comes up in rows.
stops.quote: La section argentine est une véritable création de M. Thays. Avant lui, les Argentins ignoraient complètement la flore de leur immense pays.
stops.quote_source: Jules Huret, En Argentine: de Buenos Aires au Grand Chaco (Paris: Bibliothèque-Charpentier, 1911), p. 66; a few ligature errors in the Internet Archive OCR silently corrected, wording and word order untouched, page inferred from the running heads
suggested_refs: El Yerbal, the yerba mate collection of the Jardín Botánico, raised from the 1895 germination trials
sources: Buenos Aires Botanical Garden, official history of the Yerbal collection
Jules Huret, En Argentine (1911), verified in the archive.org OCR

stops.name: Jardín Botánico, the garden opens
stops.date_confidence: attested for 7 September 1898 by both the Botanical Garden biography and the National Monuments Commission page, and Thays's own letter of 6 September 1898 announcing the opening is printed in his 1910 book and was verified here in the Internet Archive scan
stops.campa: Six years after the first letter he writes to another intendente, Alcobendas, to say the planting is nearly finished and the place can be opened. It opens on the seventh of September: seven and a half hectares carrying a Roman garden, a French garden and a picturesque one, the systematic beds of the botanists, and a section of the flora of Argentina larger than any collector in the country had thought worth assembling. He goes on living on the grounds while the trees fill in.
stops.quote: Encontrándose á punto de terminarse la plantación é instalación del Jardín Botánico, considero que, á fines del corriente mes, dicho Establecimiento podrá ser visitado por el público, en las condiciones y horas que determine la Superioridad.
stops.quote_source: Carlos Thays to Intendente Francisco P. Alcobendas, expediente 2989 D.1898, 6 September 1898, reproduced in El Jardín botánico de Buenos Aires (1910); ligature errors in the OCR silently corrected
suggested_refs: Expediente 2989 D.1898, the opening notice, printed in the Antecedentes justificativos of the 1910 book
sources: Buenos Aires Botanical Garden, 'Biografía Julio Carlos Thays'
argentina.gob.ar, 'Jardín Botánico Carlos Thays'
Carlos Thays, El Jardín botánico de Buenos Aires (1910)

stops.name: Parque Urquiza, Paraná: the park above the river
stops.date_confidence: the authorship is attested: the es.wikipedia article on Parque Urquiza credits the plan to Thays and the planting to the gardener Julio Kumagae, and dates the donation of the land to January 1894. The dossier's 1895 inauguration is supported by nothing reached, the Paraná municipal page and the academia.edu study both returned HTTP 403, and the article publishes no coordinates, so the pin is unverified
stops.campa: Paraná gives its riverside slope to the city and asks for a park on it: forty-four hectares of barranca falling to the water, the widest view in the province. The land is donated in January 1894. Thays draws the park and the gardener Julio Kumagae plants it, an arrangement that repeats through the provincial work and is usually forgotten in favour of the signature on the plan. Municipal engineers set the levels. No source reached fixes the day it opened, or says whether Thays ever stood on the slope.
suggested_refs: The planting record of Julio Kumagae at Parque Urquiza, Paraná
sources: es.wikipedia.org, 'Parque Urquiza (Paraná)'
Buenos Aires Botanical Garden, 'Biografía Julio Carlos Thays'
inaccessible: the Paraná municipal page and the academia.edu study, both HTTP 403

stops.name: Parque del Oeste, Mendoza: a design made of water
stops.date_confidence: attested by the government of Mendoza's own architectural history of the park: Ley 19 of 6 November 1896, plans presented 10 November 1896, 394 hectares. Coordinates corrected to the es.wikipedia figure; the dossier's pair lies some 750 m northeast, near the eastern gates
stops.campa: Provincial Law 19 authorizes a great park on the desert edge west of the city, and Thays has plans on the table four days later. What he draws is 394 hectares of irrigated ground in a place that takes almost no rain: the whole design is a water design, ditches and canals feeding avenues and a lake, laid over the acequia network the Huarpe dug before the Spanish arrived and the Spanish kept using. In 1910 the province buys the hill to the west, the Cerro del Pilar, and the park climbs it.
suggested_refs: Ley 19 of Mendoza, 6 November 1896, and the Huarpe acequia system beneath the park
sources: Government of Mendoza, 'La historia arquitectónica del Parque General San Martín' (mendoza.gov.ar)
es.wikipedia.org, 'Parque General San Martín'

stops.name: Estancia La Paz, Ascochinga
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1901 by La Nación, 'Los veranos cordobeses de Julio Argentino Roca'; month and day default to 01. The coordinate is the pin already carried for La Paz in this atlas and differs by some 5 km from the dossier's own figure for Ascochinga, which was not resolved here
stops.campa: Sixty kilometres north of Córdoba, in the Sierras Chicas, he lays out the park of the estancia where Julio Argentino Roca spends his summers. Roca sits between his two presidencies; the land his campaign opened in the south is in large lots now, in the hands of the men who took it and the men who financed it, and the gardens go in on top. Thays works for that class throughout: Hileret sugar in Tucumán, Tornquist at Sierra de la Ventana, Ferreyra in Córdoba, Guerrico and Güiraldes at Areco.
suggested_refs: Estancia La Paz, Ascochinga, and the park laid out by Thays in 1901
sources: La Nación, 'Los veranos cordobeses de Julio Argentino Roca'
julio_argentino_roca.journey.json

stops.name: La Porteña, San Antonio de Areco
stops.date_confidence: the commission is attested by the es.wikipedia list of Thays's works, dated there to about 1910; month and day default to 01. The estancia's association with Ricardo Güiraldes's Don Segundo Sombra is carried by the dossier and confirmed by no source reached, and the coordinates, some 5 km northwest of the town centre, could not be checked against the estate itself
stops.campa: On the pampa northwest of Buenos Aires he lays out the grounds of La Porteña for the Guerrico and Güiraldes family. Ricardo Güiraldes is said to have written Don Segundo Sombra out of this house, though no source reached here confirms it. It is the ordinary shape of the private practice in these years, fitted between municipal projects and paid for by the same families whose plazas he is building in town: an avenue of approach, a park around the house, exotic trees standing in country that grew none of them.
suggested_refs: Estancia La Porteña, San Antonio de Areco, later associated with Ricardo Güiraldes's Don Segundo Sombra
sources: es.wikipedia.org, 'Carlos Thays'
gap flagged: the Don Segundo Sombra association appears only in the dossier

segments.name: Across the River and Up the Coast

stops.name: São Luís do Maranhão, a plan sent north
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The dossier cites a notice in the Diário do Maranhão of 1901 and a USP article; the article page returned only its title when fetched and the newspaper was not reached. Whether Thays travelled to Maranhão or only posted drawings is not established, so the pin marks the plaza and not a documented presence
stops.campa: The mayor of a Brazilian port two degrees south of the equator writes to the director of the Buenos Aires botanical garden, and back comes a plan for the Largo do Palacio and the ramp down to the water. The drawings are reportedly put on public view in the city and partly built. The practice by this point runs on paper, mailed out of Palermo and executed by whoever is already there. Did the designer ever stand on that ground? Nothing reachable says either way.
suggested_refs: The Diário do Maranhão notice of 1901 on the Praça Pedro II plan, not consulted directly
sources: dossier citation of a 1901 Diário do Maranhão notice and USP scholarship
inaccessible: the USP article body text, which returned only its title

stops.name: Parque Urbano, Montevideo: the delineation and the ornament
stops.date_confidence: the Montevideo municipal page attests only that Thays intervened in the delineation and ornamentation of the Parque Urbano, the Parque Batlle, the Plaza Independencia and Carrasco, and gives no dates whatever. The 1907 here orders the segment and has no source behind it; the dossier's 1905-1912 span is likewise unsourced. Coordinates corrected to the es.wikipedia figure for Parque Rodó
stops.campa: Montevideo has the same problem as Buenos Aires and solves it the same way, by hiring the Frenchman across the river. The municipal record gives no date for the work, and no description of it beyond a single line. He works on the delineation and the ornamentation of the Parque Urbano on the coast, later renamed for José Enrique Rodó. The Plata is a hundred kilometres wide here, and the two capitals face each other across it with one climate between them and one office drawing for both.
suggested_refs: The Montevideo municipal record of Thays's interventions, municipioe.montevideo.gub.uy
sources: municipioe.montevideo.gub.uy/node/200
es.wikipedia.org, 'Parque Rodó'

stops.name: Parque Batlle y Ordóñez, Montevideo
stops.date_confidence: the involvement is attested only as intervino en la delineacion y ornamentacion on the Montevideo municipal page, with no date and no description of the work. The year orders the segment. Coordinates corrected to the es.wikipedia figure; the dossier's pair sits some 630 m northwest
stops.campa: The Parque Central, inland from the coast, is the other of Montevideo's two great parks, and he has a hand in it too. That is the standing condition of the foreign work: the plan carries his name, the execution belongs to engineers and gardeners whose names survive in payrolls, and no document reached here separates the two. The municipal record of what his hand did in this park comes to a single verb. Intervino. He intervened, in the delineation and the ornamentation.
suggested_refs: Plaza Independencia, Montevideo, listed in the same municipal record of Thays's interventions
sources: municipioe.montevideo.gub.uy/node/200
es.wikipedia.org, 'Parque Batlle'

stops.name: Carrasco, Montevideo: the suburb against the grid
stops.date_confidence: the plan for Carrasco is attested by the Montevideo municipal page, which gives no date; the year is an ordering device. That the suburb later named a plaza for him is attested on the same page
stops.campa: East of the city, on sand and pine, a resort suburb is laid out for people arriving by tram and by steamer, and Thays draws it picturesque: curved streets set against the checkerboard, blocks broken up, green left in the gaps. It is the same move he will make at Palermo Chico in Buenos Aires. A street plan outlasts a planting, since it cannot be dug up and put back differently. The Montevideo municipal record gives the drawing no date at all. The suburb keeps a plaza with his name on it, laid out long afterwards by another architect.
suggested_refs: Plaza Carlos Thays, Carrasco, Montevideo, laid out later by the architect Rubén Dufau
sources: municipioe.montevideo.gub.uy/node/200

segments.name: Iguazú and the Argument for National Parks

stops.name: Cataratas del Iguazú, the survey
stops.date_confidence: the 1902 survey at the national government's request is attested by the National Parks Administration's history page and by es.wikipedia, which credits the Ministry of the Interior. The precise arrival of 6 April, the two-month stay, and Governor Juan Jose Lanusse as co-commissioner appear in no source reached; the month is the dossier's, carried here as reconstruction, with the day defaulted to 01
stops.campa: The national government sends him to the far northeast, where the Iguazú goes over a basalt lip in hundreds of separate falls and the forest around it is being sold off in lots. He is fifty-two, eleven years into the Buenos Aires department. He walks the ground, maps the approaches, and marks where footbridges and viewpoints and a settlement could go. What he comes back arguing for, that the falls and the forest around them be kept whole and out of private hands, the country has no law for yet.
suggested_refs: The 1902 Iguazú survey commissioned by the national government
sources: National Parks Administration, official history (argentina.gob.ar/parquesnacionales)
es.wikipedia.org, 'Cataratas del Iguazú'

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the report on a national park
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1912 by the National Parks Administration history page; es.wikipedia dates the detailed survey to March 1912 and says the report carried 103 photographs. The dossier's naming of Agriculture Minister Adolfo Mujica as its recipient appears in no source reached and is dropped; the day defaults to 01
stops.campa: Ten years after the survey he hands the government a report titled Parque Nacional del Iguazú: roads, bridges, viewpoints, lodging, a hundred and three photographs of water and forest. He goes over the ground again that March, in detail, before writing any of it down. The national lands around the falls were already reserved by law in 1909, and the reserve now needs a reason to exist and a plan for what people would do inside it. His answer is that visitors will pay for preservation. He is sixty-two.
suggested_refs: Carlos Thays, Parque Nacional del Iguazú, report of 1912 with 103 photographs
sources: National Parks Administration, official history (argentina.gob.ar/parquesnacionales)
es.wikipedia.org, 'Cataratas del Iguazú'

stops.name: Paris, the international forestry congress
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The lecture and the 47-page pamphlet Les forêts naturelles de la République Argentine: projets de parcs nationaux, published through the Touring-Club de France, come from es.wikipedia cross-referenced with a WorldCat record that was not fetched; the venue address was confirmed by no page reached. Moreno's donation of 6 November 1903 is attested by the National Parks history page
stops.campa: Twenty-four years after he sailed, he stands up in Paris at an international forestry congress to talk about the natural forests of the Argentine Republic and the parks that ought to be cut out of them: Iguazú in the northeast, Nahuel Huapi in the south, where Francisco Moreno had handed the state three square leagues in 1903 to be consecrated as a public natural park. He is sixty-three, and it is the last thing he does in an official capacity. The lecture is printed as a pamphlet of forty-seven pages, in French, by the Touring-Club de France.
suggested_refs: Carlos Thays, Les forêts naturelles de la République Argentine: projets de parcs nationaux (Touring-Club de France, 1913)
sources: es.wikipedia.org, 'Carlos Thays'
National Parks Administration, official history
not fetched: the WorldCat record for the pamphlet

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the caricature in Caras y Caretas
stops.date_confidence: the caricature is attested: Caras y Caretas number 169, 28 December 1901, drawn by José María Cao Luaces, per the Wikimedia file record, and the issue number agrees with the magazine's weekly sequence. That the epithet el jardinero de la Nación derives from this image is not attested: the file record carries no such caption, and the derivation is reconstruction
stops.campa: José María Cao, a Galician draughtsman who has made himself the caricaturist of Buenos Aires, puts Thays into number 169 of Caras y Caretas on the Saturday after Christmas. The magazine reaches every waiting room in the country. Whether the phrase comes out of this drawing or only out of the years around it, no caption on the record says. It follows him for the rest of his life and long past it, one Frenchman credited with the work of several thousand municipal labourers: el jardinero de la Nación.
suggested_refs: José María Cao's caricature of Thays, Caras y Caretas no. 169, 28 December 1901
sources: Wikimedia Commons image record, 'Carlos Thays Caras y caretas.jpg'
reconstruction flagged: the epithet's derivation from the caricature is uncited

stops.name: Parque Patricios, the park on the slaughterhouse ground
stops.date_confidence: attested by es.wikipedia, which has Thays presenting the plan under the title Parque Patricios in March 1902 and the park inaugurated the same month; the day defaults to 01. Coordinates corrected: the dossier's pair sits roughly 700 m southeast of the park bounded by Caseros, Monteagudo, Uspallata and Almafuerte. The yellow fever monument stands in the adjacent Parque Ameghino, not here
stops.campa: The Matadero de los Corrales has stood on this ground since 1872, killing the city's meat in the open where the southern districts can smell it. In 1902 it closes and moves out. Thays presents a plan under the name Parque Patricios in March and the park is inaugurated the same month, on ground the working quarters had been promised for a generation. The two sites are almost always told as one story. The yellow fever dead of 1871 lie under the next park over, Ameghino, not under this one.
stops.quote: ...tendió jardines sobre todo los espacios libres, hasta a lo largo de las avenidas. Allí donde se encontraba un terreno utilizable, aunque fuera de menos de diez metros de ancho, allí, minucioso como un japonés, aparecía Mr. Thays con sus obreros, a transformarlo en umbría armoniosa.
stops.quote_source: Augusto Bunge, 'El anticarrasco,' Revista Nosotros, año X, tomo XXI (January 1916), pp. 75-76, as cited on the Spanish Wikipedia article on Thays; the journal itself was not reached and the wording is unverified
suggested_refs: The Matadero de los Corrales, 1872-1902, and the adjacent Parque Ameghino with its yellow fever monument

stops.name: Parque de la Independencia, Rosario: the park nobody can prove he drew
stops.date_confidence: the attribution is genuinely contested and is not resolved here. es.wikipedia lists the park among Thays's works and also states that the attribution has no documentary backing in specialist historical studies, which credit Mayor Luis Lamas and the municipal engineering office instead. The inauguration of 1 January 1902 is attested. The dispute is left open. Coordinates corrected: the dossier's pair lies about a kilometre west
stops.campa: Rosario opens its Parque de la Independencia on the first day of the year, the largest public work the town has attempted. Municipal tourism has credited the plan to Thays ever since. Specialist urban history answers that no document supports the credit and points instead to the mayor, Luis Lamas, and to the municipal engineering office. Nobody has produced a drawing with his signature on it, and none against it either. Whose park this is remains open.
suggested_refs: The Roldan and Godoy study disputing the Thays attribution at Rosario, not fetched for this journey

stops.name: Municipalidad de Buenos Aires, the Comisión del Plano
stops.date_confidence: attested by the Botanical Garden biography page for 6 July 1908 and the appointment by Intendente Manuel Güiraldes; the pin is the civic core, no address surviving for the office
stops.campa: Intendente Manuel Güiraldes names him to the commission drafting a plan for the whole city: traffic, sanitation, beautification, all of it at once, with the centennial of the revolution eighteen months away and Buenos Aires meaning to be looked at. He is the parks man on a body of engineers and lawyers. Seventeen years into the job, he argues about street widths and drainage as readily as about trees. The appointment is dated the sixth of July, 1908.
suggested_refs: The Comisión del Plano de Buenos Aires, 1908, and its centennial brief
sources: Buenos Aires Botanical Garden, 'Biografía Julio Carlos Thays'

stops.name: Plaza del Congreso, the paths laid to meet a bronze
stops.date_confidence: the Thinker's inauguration in November 1907 is attested; Thays's redesign of the plaza is dated to the 1910 centennial, with month and day defaulted to 01. Clemenceau's portrait was verified in three archive.org scans of the authorized English translation, South America To-day (1911); the French original was not seen, so the Spanish version in circulation is a translation of a translation
stops.campa: A cast of Rodin's Thinker was set up in the eastern half of the plaza in November 1907, signed by the sculptor's own hand, facing the parliament. It is the standing condition of the municipal work: the monuments arrive first, chosen by other men in other rooms, and the ground is arranged afterwards to make sense of them. Thays redesigns the plaza around this one for the centennial, laying paths and lawns and beds out to meet a bronze already bolted to its pedestal.
stops.quote: Apart from these plans of conquest which make him a rival of Alexander, M. Thays is a modest, affable man who takes a good deal of trouble to look as if he had done nothing out of the common.
stops.quote_source: Georges Clemenceau, South America To-day (1911), the authorized English translation of Notes de voyage dans l'Amérique du Sud, chapter 'Montevideo and Buenos Ayres', pp. 39-40
suggested_refs: The Buenos Aires cast of Rodin's Thinker, inaugurated in the Plaza del Congreso, November 1907

stops.name: Buenos Aires, El Jardín botánico de Buenos Aires
stops.date_confidence: attested and directly verified: the Internet Archive record gives J. Peuser, Buenos Aires, 1910, 180 pages, Spanish, digitized 14 May 2008 from a University of Illinois copy. Month and day default to 01. No translation into another language was located, which is an argument from silence and is stated as one
stops.campa: For the centennial the municipality prints his book on the garden through the Peuser press: a hundred and eighty pages, illustrated, with the administrative record appended at the back, his 1892 letter to Bollini and his 1898 letter to Alcobendas set out in full so that anybody can check the dates against him. It is the only one of his works he writes a book about. He says in it that he laid the ground out in three styles, symmetrical, mixed and picturesque, so that the plan itself would teach.
stops.quote: Deseando que el trazado mismo del Jardín constituyera elementos de instrucción, dispuse el trazado de modo que en él fuesen representados los tres estilos adoptados en la arquitectura paisajista, es decir: el estilo simétrico, el mixto y el pintoresco.
stops.quote_source: Carlos Thays, El Jardín botánico de Buenos Aires (Buenos Aires: Jacobo Peuser, 1910), p. 24; a few ligature errors in the Internet Archive OCR silently corrected, wording and word order untouched
suggested_refs: Eduardo Olivera's signed preface to the 1910 book, comparing Thays's work to Alphand's in Paris

stops.name: San Miguel de Tucumán, the foundation stone
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1910 by the argentina.gob.ar monuments page for Parque 9 de Julio, with month and day defaulted to 01; the same page gives the 400-hectare plan, the reclaimed swampy site, the 1916 inauguration and the fact that only the northern half was built
stops.campa: The foundation stone goes down for a park of four hundred hectares on the swampy lowland east of Tucumán, to be drained and planted for the centennial. The southern half of the drawing stays a drawing, which is the ordinary fate of the provincial commissions and is almost never mentioned beside them. It opens in 1916 for the other centennial, of the independence declared in this city in 1816, and takes the name Parque 9 de Julio. Only the northern half is there.
suggested_refs: Parque 9 de Julio, San Miguel de Tucumán, of which only the northern half of the Thays plan was executed

stops.name: Palermo Chico, the streets that refuse the grid
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1912 by the Historical Archive project inventory and by es.wikipedia; month and day default to 01. Huret's book is dated 1911, a year before this stop, and the passage was verified against two independent archive.org scans, one of which drops the word cents from quatre cents rues
stops.campa: North of Palermo a new neighbourhood is laid out for people with money and motor cars, and Thays draws it against the checkerboard the entire city is built on: small irregular blocks, curved streets, gardens in the gaps, a plan that cannot be extended by simply adding another square to the edge. Buenos Aires is a grid by law and by habit. Here, across a few hectares, it stops being one, and the street lines stay where he puts them. The quarter fills up with embassies and large houses.
stops.quote: M. Thays est demeuré un bon Français de cœur, mais veut mourir en Argentine, où il est aimé et apprécié à sa juste valeur. Avant lui, le soleil régnait en maître le long de toutes les voies publiques; il dessina tous ces squares, toutes ces places qu'il planta d'arbres; il mit de la verdure dans près de quatre cents rues, en un mot il créa l'ombre à Buenos-Aires.
stops.quote_source: Jules Huret, En Argentine: de Buenos Aires au Grand Chaco (Paris, 1911), p. 67; ligature errors in the OCR silently corrected, page inferred from the running heads, and quatre cents confirmed against a second, independent scan
suggested_refs: Barrio Parque (Palermo Chico), the irregular street plan of 1912
sources: Buenos Aires Historical Archive project inventory

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the Boy Scouts founded
stops.date_confidence: attested by the Buenos Aires Historical Archive for 4 July 1912; no source reached names the building where the founding meeting was held, so the pin is the canonical city point
stops.campa: He signs on with Francisco P. Moreno and others to found the Asociación de Boy Scouts Argentinos, an English import four years old at that point. Moreno is the man who gave the state the land at Nahuel Huapi in 1903. Thays is the man arguing for a national park at Iguazú. What the two of them are founding is a machine for taking city boys outdoors, and it belongs to the same argument as the parks: that the forests and the mountains of the country have a use which is not lumber. No source reached names the building they met in.

stops.name: Municipalidad de Buenos Aires, the end of the directorship
stops.date_confidence: both Buenos Aires municipal pages give fines de 1913, so the day is set to 31 December purely to order the segment. The es.wikipedia infobox runs the directorship to 1920; that terminus belongs to his son Carlos León Thays, who held the post from 1920, with Carrasco in between from 1914 to 1918, so the contradiction resolves as a father and son conflation rather than standing open
stops.campa: At the end of 1913 he leaves the office he has held for twenty-two years. No dismissal is recorded, no scandal, no political motive: the record simply stops. He is sixty-four, and goes into private practice, drawing estancia parks and private gardens for the families whose public plazas he had already built. Benito Carrasco, who wrote his agronomy thesis under him inside the botanical garden in 1900, runs the department from 1914 to 1918 and builds the Rosedal.
stops.quote: En el espacio de diez y nueve años que han corrido, desde su nombramiento, ha proyectado y llevado á cabo la formación de más de ochenta Parques y Paseos públicos en la ciudad de Buenos Aires...
stops.quote_source: Eduardo Olivera, preface to Carlos Thays, El Jardín botánico de Buenos Aires (1910), p. 9; ligature errors in the OCR silently corrected

stops.name: Palacio Ferreyra, Córdoba: the last of the province
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1913 by the es.wikipedia list of Thays's works; month and day default to 01
stops.campa: In Córdoba, a quarter of a century after the park that brought him to the country, he lays out the garden of the Ferreyra family's palace in Nueva Córdoba, the same expansion Miguel Crisol was selling off in lots in 1889. The house will become a museum. The garden goes in about a kilometre from the ground of his first Argentine commission, on land that was the edge of town when he arrived and is the middle of it now. The plans are dated 1913, the year he leaves the municipality.
suggested_refs: Palacio Ferreyra, Nueva Córdoba, later the Museo Superior de Bellas Artes Evita

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the death
stops.date_confidence: attested for 31 January 1934 by the Buenos Aires Historical Archive, which gives his age as 85; arithmetic from the documented birth date of 20 August 1849 gives 84 completed years. The two figures are left standing side by side and attributed. No cause of death was found in any source reached
stops.campa: He dies in Buenos Aires on the last day of January, 1934. No cause of death appears in any source reached. Born in Paris in August 1849, he is eighty-four by the arithmetic; the city's own historical archive says eighty-five, and neither figure has been reconciled with the other. He had lived in Argentina for forty-four years, longer than he ever lived in France. Twenty-three years earlier he had told a French journalist that he stayed a good Frenchman at heart but meant to die in this country.
suggested_refs: Huret's 1911 report of Thays's intention to die in Argentina
sources: Buenos Aires Historical Archive, 'Quién fue Carlos Thays'

stops.name: Cementerio de la Chacarita, the burial
stops.date_confidence: the burial at Chacarita is given by his own es.wikipedia article and by La Nación, which was unreachable during this research; the es.wikipedia article on the cemetery does not list him among its notable burials. Coordinates corrected to the es.wikipedia figure for the cemetery, both of the dossier's own pairs falling outside the grounds. Karman's eulogy comes at third hand and its wording is unverified
stops.campa: He is buried at Chacarita, the great municipal cemetery on ninety-five hectares of the city's western ground, opened for the yellow fever dead of 1871 and kept for everybody since. La Nación reports that a multitude accompanied the remains, officials and aristocrats and students and workmen walking together. The architect René Karman speaks at the graveside. Neither the plot nor the present condition of the marker could be established from anything reachable.
stops.quote: Charles Thays, del que no relataré su obra inmensa, nos deja el ejemplo de una vida toda de labor y de acción al servicio de un talento y un gusto iluminados...
stops.quote_source: René Karman, graveside eulogy, as reported in Le Courrier de la Plata (Buenos Aires), 3 February 1934, cited on the Spanish Wikipedia article on Thays; the newspaper issue was not reached and the wording is unverified

stops.name: Cataratas del Iguazú, the law arrives
stops.date_confidence: attested by the National Parks Administration history page: Law 12,103 of 29 September 1934, creating the Administración General de Parques Nacionales y Turismo and establishing Iguazú and Nahuel Huapi; the same page gives the 1928 purchase of 75,000 hectares
stops.campa: Eight months after the funeral, Law 12,103 creates the Administración General de Parques Nacionales y Turismo and establishes by statute the two parks he had argued for, Iguazú and Nahuel Huapi. The state had already bought seventy-five thousand hectares around the falls in 1928, half for a park and half for a military colony on the border. The falls he walked in 1902 are a national park by act of Congress. Thirty-two years lie between the survey and the law.
suggested_refs: Law 12,103 of 29 September 1934, founding the Argentine national parks administration

stops.name: Jardín Botánico, the garden takes his name
stops.date_confidence: attested for 31 August 1937 by es.wikipedia's article on the Jardín Botánico Carlos Thays; the argentina.gob.ar page cited for it in the dossier does not in fact contain the naming date, and that misattribution is corrected here. The bust and plaque are catalogued on Wikimedia Commons with neither sculptor nor unveiling date
stops.campa: Three and a half years after the funeral the city officially puts his name on the Palermo garden. The garden is thirty-nine years old that August, and the trees standing in it are his. A bust of him and a commemorative plaque stand inside the grounds, sculptor and installation date unrecorded by any source reached. It is the work he proposed himself, in writing, in 1892, and the only one whose entire administrative paper trail he printed in his own lifetime, so that the authorship could not be argued about afterwards.

stops.name: Jardín Botánico, declared a national monument
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1996 by the argentina.gob.ar National Monuments Commission page, which cites Decreto 366/1996; month and day are not given there and default to 01
stops.campa: Decreto 366 of 1996 declares the garden a monumento histórico nacional: the seven and a half hectares, the 1881 casona the family lived in, the greenhouses, the plane trees now a century into the ground. A decree can protect a plan, which is a document. The collection is alive, and has to be replanted generation after generation by people who never met the man whose name is on the gate. Some of the oldest specimens went into the ground under his orders.

stops.name: Parque Carlos Thays, Recoleta
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1998 by es.wikipedia's article on Parque Thays, with the Italpark closure of 1990 after a fatal ride accident; month and day default to 01. The saying quoted here is ubiquitous in Argentine commemorative and tourism writing and has no located first publication, so it is carried as traditional attribution and not as a documented quotation
stops.campa: At Libertador and Callao, on the ground where the Italpark amusement park stood until a fatal accident on a ride closed it in 1990, the city opens four and a half thousand square metres of park and puts his name on it. He did not design it. He had been dead sixty-four years. The name has become a municipal category by this point, attached to green space in general rather than to any drawing he ever made. A Botero torso stands in the middle of it. The line Argentine commemorative writing keeps putting in his mouth, that it is better to live in a cabin in a wood than a palace without a garden, has never been traced to anything he published.
stops.quote: Para ser feliz, es preferible vivir en una cabaña dentro de un bosque que en un palacio sin jardín.
stops.quote_source: Attributed to Thays throughout Argentine commemorative and tourism writing; no contemporaneous publication of the line was located, and it is carried here as traditional attribution
suggested_refs: Parque Thays, Recoleta, on the former site of the Italpark

stops.name: Archivo Histórico de la Ciudad, the papers come in
stops.date_confidence: attested for 2014 by the city's own notice of the incorporation of the donated Archivo Carlos Thays; month and day are not given and default to 01. The dates for the son are the family firm's own: Carlos León Thays, 1894-1962, director general de paseos from 1920 to 1945
stops.campa: His heirs give the city the Archivo Carlos Thays: plans and projects for public and private commissions across the Argentine provinces and for work in France, Chile and Uruguay, personal papers, photographs, and the drawings of his son Carlos León, who ran the same municipal department from 1920 to 1945. The confusion between the two men, and with the grandson Carlos Julio, has been shifting credit around inside one family for a century. Against these papers it can be checked. The donation is catalogued in 2014.
